# Configuration reference

<!-- Generated by `python -m cryo.capabilities.generate_config_reference`;
do not edit. -->

Every environment variable Cryo reads, and every top-level Helm value the chart
accepts.

## Environment variables

Cryo reads these from the environment, with the `CRYO_` prefix. A default of
*(set from a secret)*, *(unset)* or *(computed)* means there is no safe default to
print.

| Variable | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CRYO_APP_NAME` | `str` | `Cryo` | - |
| `CRYO_ENVIRONMENT` | `Literal` | `dev` | - |
| `CRYO_DATABASE_URL` | `str` | *(set from a secret)* | Holds a credential. Set it from a secret store, never from a committed file. - |
| `CRYO_REDIS_URL` | `str` | *(set from a secret)* | Holds a credential. Set it from a secret store, never from a committed file. - |
| `CRYO_SECRET_KEY` | `str` | *(set from a secret)* | Holds a credential. Set it from a secret store, never from a committed file. - |
| `CRYO_SECRET_KEY_PREVIOUS` | `str \| None` | *(unset)* | Holds a credential. Set it from a secret store, never from a committed file. Key stored secrets were encrypted with before a rotation. Decryption tries secret_key first, then this; `cryo rotate-secret-key` re-encrypts with secret_key, after which this can be removed. It may be the old default. |
| `CRYO_JWT_SECRET` | `str \| None` | *(set from a secret)* | Holds a credential. Set it from a secret store, never from a committed file. HS256 secret for API JWTs. Defaults to secret_key when unset. |
| `CRYO_ENFORCE_TENANT_ISOLATION` | `bool` | `false` | When true, every JWT must carry tenant_id and queries are scoped. |
| `CRYO_OIDC_ISSUER_URL` | `str \| None` | *(unset)* | OIDC issuer URL (production SSO). Enables RS256 IdP token verification. |
| `CRYO_OIDC_CLIENT_ID` | `str \| None` | *(unset)* | OIDC OAuth client id. |
| `CRYO_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET` | `str \| None` | *(set from a secret)* | Holds a credential. Set it from a secret store, never from a committed file. OIDC client secret for authorization-code exchange. |
| `CRYO_OIDC_AUDIENCE` | `str \| None` | *(unset)* | Expected access-token audience; defaults to oidc_client_id. |
| `CRYO_OIDC_JWKS_URI` | `str \| None` | *(unset)* | Optional JWKS URI override (defaults to issuer/.well-known/jwks.json). |
| `CRYO_OIDC_REDIRECT_URI` | `str \| None` | *(unset)* | OAuth redirect URI registered with the IdP (UI callback). |
| `CRYO_ALLOW_DEV_TOKEN_IN_PROD` | `bool` | `false` | Explicit opt-in to keep POST /api/v1/auth/token (self-declared role, no real identity check) enabled even when environment=='prod'. Only for bridging the gap before OIDC is configured -- anyone who can reach the API can self-grant any role while this is true. Turn off once oidc_issuer_url is set. |
| `CRYO_GOOGLE_ADMIN_EMAILS` | `str` | `""` | Comma-separated Google emails that become Cryo admins on their first Google sign-in when no Cryo user exists for them. Bootstraps the first admin once Google sign-in is enabled and dev tokens are turned off. Does not change the role of an existing user. |
| `CRYO_CORS_ALLOW_ORIGINS` | `list` | *(computed)* | - |
| `CRYO_SCAN_NUM_CHUNKS` | `int` | `4` | - |
| `CRYO_SCAN_SMALL_FILE_MB` | `float` | `89.6` | - |
| `CRYO_SCAN_NEEDS_COMPACTION_THRESHOLD` | `int` | `128` | - |
| `CRYO_REPORT_COST_DOD_SPIKE_PCT` | `float` | `10.0` | Day-over-day fleet cost increase (%) that flags a spike. |
| `CRYO_REPORT_COST_DOD_DECLINE_PCT` | `float` | `30.0` | Day-over-day fleet cost decrease (%) that flags a decline worth noting. |
| `CRYO_REPORT_COST_WOW_SPIKE_PCT` | `float` | `15.0` | Week-over-week fleet cost increase (%) that flags a spike. |
| `CRYO_REPORT_COST_WOW_DECLINE_PCT` | `float` | `35.0` | Week-over-week fleet cost decrease (%) that flags a decline worth noting. |
| `CRYO_REPORT_QUERY_COST_DOD_SPIKE_PCT` | `float` | `15.0` | Day-over-day Trino query cost increase (%) that flags a spike. |
| `CRYO_REPORT_QUERY_COST_DOD_DECLINE_PCT` | `float` | `30.0` | Day-over-day Trino query cost decrease (%) that flags a decline worth noting. |
| `CRYO_REPORT_QUERY_COST_WOW_SPIKE_PCT` | `float` | `20.0` | Week-over-week Trino query cost increase (%) that flags a spike. |
| `CRYO_REPORT_QUERY_COST_WOW_DECLINE_PCT` | `float` | `35.0` | Week-over-week Trino query cost decrease (%) that flags a decline. |
| `CRYO_REPORT_IMPACT_DOD_MOVE_PCT` | `float` | `25.0` | Day-over-day change (%) in GB reclaimed that's worth flagging either way. |
| `CRYO_REPORT_IMPACT_WOW_MOVE_PCT` | `float` | `20.0` | Week-over-week change (%) in GB reclaimed that's worth flagging either way. |
| `CRYO_SHARED_S3_REPORT_ENABLED` | `bool` | `false` | Post the shared-S3-path anomaly report to Slack. |
| `CRYO_QUERY_COST_REPORT_ENABLED` | `bool` | `false` | Post the Trino query-cost report to Slack. |
| `CRYO_PRODUCTION_HEALTH_CHECK_ENABLED` | `bool` | `false` | Post the production health check to Slack. |
| `CRYO_MAINTENANCE_TOP_N` | `int` | `500` | Tables per batch run. |
| `CRYO_MAINTENANCE_DESTINATION_ID` | `str \| None` | *(unset)* | Spark destination to run on; defaults to the only enabled Spark one. |
| `CRYO_MAINTENANCE_MAX_LANES` | `int` | `4` | Max Spark pods. |
| `CRYO_MAINTENANCE_LANE_MAX_CPU_MILLI` | `int` | `4000` | - |
| `CRYO_MAINTENANCE_LANE_MAX_MEM_MIB` | `int` | `16384` | - |
| `CRYO_MAINTENANCE_LANE_MAX_NODE_CPU` | `int` | `0` | Optional inclusive Karpenter node vCPU ceiling for maintenance lanes. Zero disables it; enabling requires karpenter.k8s.aws/instance-cpu node labels. Prevents small protected lanes from pinning very large shared nodes. |
| `CRYO_MAINTENANCE_LANE_TARGET_GB` | `float` | `200.0` | Rewrite GB one lane should carry before another pod is worth starting. |
| `CRYO_MAINTENANCE_MAX_LANE_RESPAWNS` | `int` | `8` | Replacement pods one run may start for lanes that died mid-run (OOM, node loss). The table a lane died on is recorded as failed; the replacement takes the rest. |
| `CRYO_MAINTENANCE_LANE_CAPACITY_TYPES` | `str` | `spot,on-demand` | Karpenter capacity types lane pods may run on, most preferred first. Replaces the karpenter.sh/capacity-type pin lanes inherit from the Spark destination's node selector; empty keeps that pin. Lanes tolerate node loss (partial-progress commits, replacement lanes), so they don't need the on-demand-only rule the per-statement Spark path has. |
| `CRYO_MAINTENANCE_MAX_RUNTIME_MINUTES` | `int` | `360` | Hard stop for the whole run; lanes stop starting tables 20 min earlier. |
| `CRYO_MAINTENANCE_COOLDOWN_HOURS` | `int` | `20` | - |
| `CRYO_MAINTENANCE_MAX_STATS_AGE_DAYS` | `int` | `3` | Skip tables whose last successful scan is older than this. |
| `CRYO_MAINTENANCE_SHARED_SNAPSHOT_MAX_AGE_HOURS` | `int` | `72` | If the shared-S3-path snapshot cannot be refreshed and the last one is older than this, the run skips remove_orphan_files on every table. |
| `CRYO_MAINTENANCE_MEASURE_ORPHAN_BYTES` | `bool` | `false` | Before each remove_orphan_files, run the same call as a dry run and sum the sizes of the files it lists, so orphan removal's audit rows carry actual_bytes_freed. Off by default: the dry run doubles the orphan LIST, which has OOM'd Spark before. |
| `CRYO_MAINTENANCE_AUTOCOMP_W_FILE_REDUCTION` | `float` | `0.7` | - |
| `CRYO_MAINTENANCE_AUTOCOMP_HEAT_WEIGHT` | `float` | `0.3` | Cryo extension: share of the score from Trino query heat; 0 = paper-only. |
| `CRYO_MAINTENANCE_AUTOCOMP_REWRITE_GB_PER_HOUR` | `float` | `25.0` | RewriteBytesPerHour until a run has measured it; afterwards the median of recent runs' observed rewrite throughput is used. |
| `CRYO_MAINTENANCE_DURATION_MODEL` | `Literal` | `rate` | How AutoComp estimates a table's rewrite hours. 'rate': GiB / RewriteBytesPerHour. 'ernest': the Ernest model fitted on completed rewrite statements (cryo/maintenance/ernest.py), used only while it beats 'rate' on held-out runs; the comparison is recorded in every run's autocomp trace either way. |
| `CRYO_MAINTENANCE_AUTOCOMP_BUDGET_GBHR` | `float \| None` | *(unset)* | Compute budget per scheduled run. Unset: max_lanes x lane memory x the hours lanes may start tables. |
| `CRYO_MAINTENANCE_POLL_SECONDS` | `int` | `30` | - |
| `CRYO_MAINTENANCE_RESCAN_ENABLED` | `bool` | `true` | - |
| `CRYO_MAINTENANCE_SLACK_ENABLED` | `bool` | `true` | - |
| `CRYO_MAINTENANCE_WRITES_ENABLED` | `bool` | `true` | When false, maintenance cannot enqueue or execute Iceberg writes. |
| `CRYO_SCAN_FRESHNESS_EXCLUDED_SCHEMAS` | `str` | `temp` | Comma-separated schema names excluded from scan_freshness/scan_failures (health checks) -- for scratch/staging schemas whose tables are never queried, so a slow scan cadence against them isn't a real signal. Confirmed live 2026-09-28: schema 'temp' (341 active tables) had zero query_logs rows ever, on any table, but contributed 166 of 209 scan_freshness stale-table flags purely from losing out on scan priority to tables that are actually read -- a real capacity tradeoff, not a scanner problem worth alerting on. Empty string excludes nothing. |
| `CRYO_SCAN_DEAD_TABLE_FAILURE_THRESHOLD` | `int` | `10` | consecutive_scan_failures at or above this AND zero query_logs rows in scan_dead_table_lookback_days -> auto-deactivate the table. Both conditions must hold: a table with any recent query traffic is never deactivated regardless of scan failure streak. Confirmed live 2026-09-28: 148 tables past this threshold (up to 175 consecutive failures) had zero Trino query traffic in 30 days -- stale catalog entries (deleted __dbt_tmp/backfill metadata), not live tables Cryo was failing to read. |
| `CRYO_SCAN_DEAD_TABLE_LOOKBACK_DAYS` | `int` | `30` | - |
| `CRYO_SCAN_REMOVE_MISSING_TABLES_ENABLED` | `bool` | `true` | Tombstone registry rows whose table is no longer in a complete catalog listing (#120): removed_from_catalog_at is set and the table goes inactive. Reversible: a table that shows up again is restored on the next scan. Nothing is hard-deleted. |
| `CRYO_SCAN_MISSING_TABLE_MAX_FRACTION` | `float` | `0.2` | Mass-removal guard: if one scan would remove more than this share of a source's registered tables, it removes none and records why. Ignored for at most scan_missing_table_guard_min_count removals, so small catalogs still reconcile. |
| `CRYO_SCAN_MISSING_TABLE_MAX_COUNT` | `int` | `500` | Mass-removal guard: never remove more than this many tables per source per scan; above it, remove none and record why. |
| `CRYO_SCAN_MISSING_TABLE_GUARD_MIN_COUNT` | `int` | `5` | - |
| `CRYO_DISPATCH_HEARTBEAT_STALL_MINUTES` | `int` | `1560` | Minutes since the last MaintenanceJob admitted/started/finished before vitals.dispatch_heartbeat calls dispatch stalled. Cryo's only dispatch source is the once-daily maintenance CronJob (default 26h gap, schedule permitting), not a continuously-draining queue -- this must exceed that gap plus the run's own max_runtime_minutes, or every quiet hour between runs reads as an outage. |
| `CRYO_SCAN_PARALLEL_TABLES` | `int` | `0` | Tables to scan in parallel per chunk (0=serial). |
| `CRYO_SCAN_PARALLEL_MANIFESTS` | `int` | `4` | Max threads for parallel manifest fetching within a table. Kept modest under typical 2Gi scanner-worker limits: each in-flight manifest still materializes its entry list. |
| `CRYO_SCANNER_WAIR_FILE_SAMPLE_SIZE` | `int` | `1000` | Maximum deterministic current-snapshot data-file bound samples retained per table for WAIR analysis, restricted to range-queried numeric/temporal columns. Zero disables collection. |
| `CRYO_SCAN_ENGINE` | `Literal` | `pyiceberg` | Metadata walk implementation for current-snapshot stats. 'go' shells out to cryo-engine-go scan-stats (streaming manifests); 'pyiceberg' uses the in-process path. |
| `CRYO_SCAN_GO_BINARY` | `str \| None` | *(unset)* | Optional path to cryo-engine-go; otherwise resolve like native runner. |
| `CRYO_COST_METADATA_MAX_FILES_ESTIMATE` | `int` | `2000000` | Cheap pre-filter before even attempting Tier-1 metadata cost accounting: skip it when the current-snapshot file count meets or exceeds this threshold. The real memory guard is inside account_metadata_cost itself (cost_scan_max_snapshots/cost_scan_max_manifests, checked live during the walk, with a graceful heuristic fallback either way) -- this is just an outer bound for pathological cases, not the primary defense. Confirmed live, 2026-08-03: the previous default (200_000) excluded a table with 207,511 files (24TB, ~$700/mo, the single most cost-relevant table in the fleet) from all cost/reclaim accounting -- table_cost had zero rows for it, ever -- for a file count barely above the threshold and nowhere near what the internal walk can actually handle. |
| `CRYO_COST_METADATA_MAX_MANIFESTS_CURRENT` | `int` | `500` | Skip Tier-1 metadata cost when current-snapshot manifest count meets or exceeds this threshold. |
| `CRYO_COST_PRICE_PER_GB_MONTH` | `float` | `0.023` | - |
| `CRYO_COST_USE_GIB` | `bool` | `true` | - |
| `CRYO_COST_SCAN_TIER` | `Literal` | `metadata` | - |
| `CRYO_COST_SCAN_MAX_SNAPSHOTS` | `int` | `200` | - |
| `CRYO_COST_SCAN_MAX_MANIFESTS` | `int` | `5000` | - |
| `CRYO_COST_FULL_SCAN_EVERY_HOURS` | `int` | `168` | - |
| `CRYO_COST_ORPHAN_MIN_AGE_HOURS` | `int` | `72` | - |
| `CRYO_COST_SCAN_MAX_LIST_KEYS` | `int` | `1000000` | - |
| `CRYO_DEFAULT_RETENTION_DAYS` | `int` | `7` | - |
| `CRYO_DEFAULT_RETAIN_LAST` | `int` | `1` | - |
| `CRYO_S3_GET_USD_PER_1K` | `float` | `0.0004` | - |
| `CRYO_S3_LIST_USD_PER_1K` | `float` | `0.005` | - |
| `CRYO_S3_PUT_USD_PER_1K` | `float` | `0.005` | - |
| `CRYO_QUERY_GETS_PER_FILE` | `float` | `1.0` | - |
| `CRYO_DISPLAY_TIMEZONE` | `str` | `UTC` | IANA time zone for the install (CRYO_DISPLAY_TIMEZONE), for example 'Asia/Kolkata' or 'Europe/Berlin'. Cron presets, the destination off-peak window and run report clocks all use it, so a schedule and its off-peak window always agree. Exposed to the web app via /api/v1/runtime. Before #183 the off-peak gate and reports were hard-coded to IST while cron ran in UTC; set this to 'Asia/Kolkata' to keep the old off-peak behavior. |
| `CRYO_OFFPEAK_START_IST` | `int` | `0` | - |
| `CRYO_OFFPEAK_END_IST` | `int` | `0` | - |
| `CRYO_DEFAULT_PER_REPLICA_OPTIMIZE_CAP` | `int` | `5` | - |
| `CRYO_DEFAULT_EMR_SLOT_CAP` | `int` | `10` | - |
| `CRYO_DEFAULT_NATIVE_SLOT_CAP` | `int` | `5` | - |
| `CRYO_WAVE_WAIT_SEC` | `int` | `300` | - |
| `CRYO_MAX_JOBS_PER_SCHEDULED_RUN` | `int` | `500` | Hard cap on how many tables one cron-triggered run may target. build_scheduled_run has always accepted a budget_hint, but the cron path never passed one, so a single preset fired against every matching table in the fleet. Live 2026-09-21: scheduled runs of 3,478-6,117 jobs against a worker fleet whose real ceiling is ~3,000 jobs/day, so 5,952 of 6,117 jobs in one run aged out of ADMITTED and were recorded as failures without an engine ever touching the table. Candidates are ranked by apply_priority_order before this slice, so the cap keeps the highest-value tables. With scheduler_backlog_drain_enabled this caps each batch, not the night. |
| `CRYO_SCHEDULER_BACKLOG_DRAIN_ENABLED` | `bool` | `true` | After a capped cron run, keep scheduling further batches of the preset's remaining candidates whenever the previous batch has drained, until the next cron fire. Each table is attempted at most once per cron period. A preset opts out with guardrails.backlog_drain=false. |
| `CRYO_SCHEDULER_BACKLOG_DRAIN_LOW_WATER` | `int` | `50` | Next backlog batch is scheduled once the preset has at most this many queued, admitted or running jobs. Deferred jobs are not counted: they hold no engine capacity and a few routinely stay deferred for hours. |
| `CRYO_SCHEDULER_BACKLOG_DRAIN_INTERVAL_SECONDS` | `int` | `900` | Minimum time between backlog batches of one preset. |
| `CRYO_STUCK_ADMITTED_AFTER_SECONDS` | `int` | `900` | Grace period before reconcile_stuck_admitted_jobs treats an ADMITTED job with no engine_ref as undispatched. Only applies to jobs that are genuinely absent from the claim queue; a job still waiting its turn is left alone however long the queue is. |
| `CRYO_WORKER_DISPATCH_BACKLOG_PER_REPLICA` | `int` | `3` | Admission backpressure: the governor will not grow the undispatched ADMITTED backlog beyond this many jobs per live worker replica. Engine slot_cap bounds how much load the ENGINE can take; it says nothing about how fast workers can drain the claim queue, and workers process one job at a time. Without this the governor admits against engine capacity alone and buries the claim queue under work no worker can reach inside the stuck-admitted grace period. |
| `CRYO_ENGINE_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_SEC` | `float` | `5.0` | Per-request connect timeout (seconds) for Trino coordinator probes and statement execution. The trino client doesn't expose a connect timeout directly, so we patch the requests Session it uses. |
| `CRYO_SCAN_TABLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | `float` | `180.0` | Hard wall-clock bound for scanning a single table (catalog load, stats analysis, and orphan-file listing). Catalog/S3 clients don't reliably honor their own timeouts against a slow or unresponsive Hive Metastore/S3 endpoint, so this work runs in a bounded worker and is treated as a failed scan past this limit instead of blocking the scanner daemon's single poll loop forever. |
| `CRYO_SCANNER_MAX_PARTITIONS_PER_TABLE` | `int` | `5000` | Cap on how many partition rows a single scan persists to table_partitions per table, keeping the ones with the most small files (the actual compaction signal). Real catalogs have a long tail of tables partitioned far more finely than any compaction decision needs -- one observed table had 397k partitions (median table: 8) and alone accounted for ~10% of table_partitions' total row count. |
| `CRYO_NATIVE_ENGINE_ENABLED` | `bool` | `true` | Enable native cryo-engine maintenance (default workflow). |
| `CRYO_FLINK_ENGINE_ENABLED` | `bool` | `false` | Enable Flink config-generation engine (does not submit jobs). |
| `CRYO_HILBERT_CLUSTERING_ENABLED` | `bool` | `false` | Allow Hilbert-curve clustering. Off by default: Iceberg only gained hilbert() in 1.12.0 on the Spark 4.1 path (PR #16827, merged 2026-08-25), and an unsupported runtime fails at procedure-parse time after the job is submitted. Requests downgrade to Z-order unless the versions below confirm support. |
| `CRYO_SPARK_ICEBERG_VERSION` | `str \| None` | *(unset)* | Iceberg runtime version on the Spark destination, e.g. '1.12.0'. Used to gate Hilbert clustering; unknown is treated as unsupported, never as new enough. |
| `CRYO_SPARK_RUNTIME_VERSION` | `str \| None` | *(unset)* | Spark version on the destination, e.g. '4.1.0'. Used to gate Hilbert clustering; unknown is treated as unsupported. |
| `CRYO_HEALTH_PORT` | `int` | `8081` | HTTP port for /healthz and /metrics on background services. |
| `CRYO_DAEMON_TICK_STALL_SECONDS` | `int` | `0` | Background services report unhealthy on /healthz when a single loop tick has run longer than this many seconds (0 disables the check). The Helm chart sets it per service so its liveness probe restarts a hung scheduler, worker or scanner. |
| `CRYO_TELEMETRY_INGEST_ON_STARTUP` | `bool` | `true` | When true, scheduler attempts query-log ingest ticks if configured. |
| `CRYO_TELEMETRY_TRINO_URL` | `str \| None` | *(unset)* | Trino coordinator URL for scheduled query-log ingestion (CRYO_TELEMETRY_TRINO_URL). |
| `CRYO_TELEMETRY_TRINO_USER` | `str \| None` | *(unset)* | Username for telemetry_trino_url, if the coordinator requires auth (CRYO_TELEMETRY_TRINO_USER). Defaults to 'cryo' if a password is set but no username is given. |
| `CRYO_TELEMETRY_TRINO_PASSWORD` | `str \| None` | *(unset)* | Holds a credential. Set it from a secret store, never from a committed file. Password for telemetry_trino_url, if the coordinator requires auth (CRYO_TELEMETRY_TRINO_PASSWORD). Unset means no BasicAuthentication is attempted. |
| `CRYO_TELEMETRY_TRINO_SSL_VERIFY` | `bool` | `true` | Verify TLS certificates when connecting to telemetry_trino_url (CRYO_TELEMETRY_TRINO_SSL_VERIFY). Only disable for coordinators with self-signed/internal-CA certs you've already verified out of band. |
| `CRYO_TELEMETRY_ATHENA_WORKGROUP` | `str \| None` | *(unset)* | Optional Athena workgroup filter for query-log ingestion. |
| `CRYO_S3_LOG_TRINO_CATALOG` | `str` | `hive` | Trino Hive-connector catalog/schema used only to clean up an external log table from an older Trino-based ingestion run when tearing down S3 request-cost tracking for a bucket (cryo/integrations/s3_bucket_provisioning.py). Ingestion itself reads and aggregates S3 access logs natively -- no Trino dependency. |
| `CRYO_S3_LOG_TRINO_SCHEMA` | `str` | `cryo_s3_logs` | Schema within s3_log_trino_catalog for the legacy teardown path above. |
| `CRYO_QUERY_LOG_RETENTION_DAYS` | `int` | `90` | Days of raw query_logs rows to keep before the scheduler purges them. query_patterns (the aggregated signal partition/layout recommendations actually consume) is unaffected by purging, since it's aggregated before rows age out. Default (90d) is set at or above every consumer's own lookback window (the longest being cryo/tiering/s3_analyzer.py's 90-day default) so purging never silently starves a feature of data it still needs. |
| `CRYO_AUDIT_LOG_RETENTION_DAYS` | `int` | `365` | Days to retain immutable maintenance audit entries in the operational database. The leader scheduler prunes older rows in bounded batches. Set a longer value when regulatory or incident-response policy requires it; 365 days is the safe default. |
| `CRYO_AUDIT_LOG_PRUNE_BATCH_SIZE` | `int` | `10000` | Maximum audit rows deleted in one transaction. |
| `CRYO_AUDIT_LOG_PRUNE_MAX_ROWS_PER_TICK` | `int` | `100000` | Maximum audit rows deleted by one daily leader-scheduler retention tick. |
| `CRYO_TABLE_STATS_HISTORY_RETENTION_DAYS` | `int` | `180` | Days to retain per-scan TableStatsHistory snapshots. Had no retention at all until 2026-10-05 -- one row per table per scan, every 6h (scanner.schedule), with nothing ever deleting old rows: 49GB of a 61GB production DB, 80% of the metadata database, for 853K rows. The longest real consumer lookback is 90 days (cost_model_refresh_interval_hours's build_outcome_dataset); 180 is a safety margin above that, not a measured requirement. |
| `CRYO_TABLE_STATS_HISTORY_PRUNE_BATCH_SIZE` | `int` | `10000` | Maximum table_stats_history rows deleted in one transaction. |
| `CRYO_TABLE_STATS_HISTORY_PRUNE_MAX_ROWS_PER_TICK` | `int` | `100000` | Maximum table_stats_history rows deleted by one daily retention tick. |
| `CRYO_JOB_RETENTION_DAYS` | `int` | `180` | Days to retain finished MaintenanceJob rows (status terminal, finished_at set). Had no retention at all until 2026-10-05. Only ever deletes rows with a non-null finished_at, so queued/admitted/running jobs are never eligible. |
| `CRYO_JOB_PRUNE_BATCH_SIZE` | `int` | `10000` | Maximum job rows deleted in one transaction. |
| `CRYO_JOB_PRUNE_MAX_ROWS_PER_TICK` | `int` | `100000` | Maximum job rows deleted by one daily retention tick. |
| `CRYO_QUERY_LOG_ICEBERG_WINDOW_HOURS` | `int` | `1` | Time-window size for the iceberg_table read-through query-log path (cryo/telemetry/iceberg_source.py). Each window is scanned and watermarked independently so a busy Trino cluster's query-event-listener table (which can log millions of rows over the default 7-day first-run lookback, and whose raw SQL text can be large per row) never has to be materialized into memory as one unbounded scan. Default is deliberately small (1h): measured against a real busy cluster, a single call processing 8 x 6h windows peaked at ~2.3GB, which exceeds the scheduler deployment's default 2Gi memory limit (the process that runs this automatically) even though it stayed under the API pod's 3Gi. 1h keeps per-call peak memory well under either limit; tune upward only if profiled safe for your own query volume. |
| `CRYO_QUERY_LOG_ICEBERG_MAX_WINDOWS_PER_TICK` | `int` | `4` | Max number of query_log_iceberg_window_hours windows processed per aggregation call. Bounds how much a large backlog (first-ever run, or catch-up after an outage) can do in one tick; the rest is picked up on the next scheduled tick. |
| `CRYO_QUERY_LOG_ICEBERG_MAX_ROWS_PER_WINDOW` | `int` | `25000` | Last-resort per-window row cap for the iceberg_table read-through query-log path. Only triggers if a single window still has an extreme row count; excess rows in that window are dropped (logged as a warning) rather than blocking the watermark from advancing past that window. |
| `CRYO_TELEMETRY_DUCKDB_ENABLED` | `bool` | `false` | Enable DuckDB query-log ingestion (dev-only). |

| `CRYO_OTEL_ENABLED` | `bool` | `false` | Enable OpenTelemetry tracing and OTLP export. |

| `CRYO_CREDENTIAL_VENDING_ENABLED` | `bool` | `false` | Holds a credential. Set it from a secret store, never from a committed file. Enable REST catalog STS credential vending in worker. |

| `CRYO_SMTP_USER` | `str \| None` | *(unset)* | - |
| `CRYO_SMTP_PASSWORD` | `str \| None` | *(unset)* | Holds a credential. Set it from a secret store, never from a committed file. - |

| `CRYO_SMTP_USE_TLS` | `bool` | `true` | - |

| `CRYO_ML_DRIFT_CHECK_INTERVAL_HOURS` | `int` | `24` | Hours between scheduled health-classifier drift evaluations. |
| `CRYO_UNMATCHED_TABLES_CHECK_INTERVAL_HOURS` | `int` | `6` | Hours between fleet-wide sweeps for active tables that resolve to no effective preset (cryo.scheduler.rules.effective_preset returns None) -- these are never scheduled for maintenance by any cron and previously went undetected. Matches the scanner cadence (0 */6 * * *) since that's when needs_compaction can change. Real incident, 2026-08-12: 1,267 active tables with needs_compaction=True matched no enabled preset, including a 24TB table pinned to a preset that had been disabled -- found only via manual investigation, with no metric surfacing it. |

| `CRYO_SLACK_DAILY_REPORT_ENABLED` | `bool` | `false` | Enable daily anomaly report to Slack. |
| `CRYO_SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET` | `str \| None` | *(unset)* | Holds a credential. Set it from a secret store, never from a committed file. Signing secret for Slack interactive requests. Unset rejects those requests. |
| `CRYO_COMPUTE_STATISTICS_ENABLED` | `bool` | `true` | Enable Puffin statistics computation after compaction by default. |
| `CRYO_STATS_COLUMNS_LIMIT` | `int` | `50` | Max columns to compute stats for (high-cardinality priority). |
| `CRYO_BENEFIT_SCORE_UPDATE_INTERVAL_HOURS` | `int` | `6` | Hours between AutoComp benefit score recalculations. |
| `CRYO_BENEFIT_SCORE_SWEEP_VIA_K8S_JOBS` | `bool` | `false` | Recovery plan §2/§8, 2026-09-20: when true, BenefitScoreUpdaterRunner's tick ensures a durable analysis_tasks row is due and dispatches a bounded K8s Job (cryo.analysis.dispatch) to process it, instead of running the multi-hour sweep in-process (the scheduler-OOM root cause this whole mechanism replaces). Defaults to False so upgrading this chart does not silently cut over production before the plan's required shadow-run/burn-in gate passes -- flip only after analysis.enabled is deployed and the runner has been observed clean across several real cycles. |
| `CRYO_EVOLVING_CATALOG_CLEANUP_INTERVAL_HOURS` | `int` | `6` | Hours between sweeps deactivating orphaned '*_evolving' catalog entries (cryo.db.repositories.sources.deactivate_orphaned_evolving_catalog_entries) -- the fix existed since 2026-08-26 (ace7f4b) but was never wired to a scheduled runner, so the same historical rename artifact (1,200+ tables, location IS NULL, a verified-good sibling with a real location) kept re-accumulating as the fleet's single worst repeat_failures pattern every day the cleanup wasn't run manually. |
| `CRYO_COST_MODEL_REFRESH_INTERVAL_HOURS` | `int` | `6` | Hours between cost-model retrains (cryo.ml.cost_integration.refresh_cost_model_cache). Live outage, 2026-09-10: this used to run inline, unconditionally, on every single job completion on every worker pod (cryo/worker/worker.py) -- confirmed live as the real root cause of a fleet-wide worker OOM cascade (kernel-verified via /proc/1/smaps_rollup, and independently reproduced by OOMKilling a cryo-api pod via one call to /api/v1/ai/cost-model/evaluate, same build_outcome_dataset code path -- QueryLog/TableStatsHistory/TableCostHistory/ QueryCostAttributionDaily queries over a 90-day window with no row limit on any of the secondary queries). Moved to a periodic CostModelRefreshRunner daemon, matching the same fix shape as evolving_catalog_cleanup_interval_hours above. |
| `CRYO_TRINO_HOT_PRESET_REPIN_INTERVAL_HOURS` | `int` | `24` | Hours between repins of the daily top-N-by-Trino-query-frequency maintenance preset (cryo.scheduler.trino_hot_preset.repin_trino_hot_tables) -- daily by default, matching its purpose: concentrate maintenance effort on whichever tables are actually driving Trino scan cost right now, re-evaluated once a day. |
| `CRYO_TRINO_HOT_PRESET_NAME` | `str` | `daily-trino-hot-tables` | Name of the Preset (see scripts/seed_trino_hot_preset.py) that TrinoHotPresetRunner repins daily -- must match an existing, seeded Preset.name. |
| `CRYO_TRINO_HOT_PRESET_TABLE_LIMIT` | `int` | `500` | How many top-Trino-query-frequency tables to pin to the preset each repin. |
| `CRYO_API_RATE_LIMIT_RPS` | `float` | `0.5` | Token refill rate for expensive API endpoints (requests/sec). |
| `CRYO_API_RATE_LIMIT_BURST` | `int` | `10` | Burst capacity for expensive API endpoint rate limiting. |
| `CRYO_AUTH_LOGIN_THROTTLE_ENABLED` | `bool` | `true` | Throttle failed password and Google sign-ins per account and per client IP. Counters live in Redis so the limit holds across API replicas. |
| `CRYO_AUTH_LOGIN_MAX_FAILURES` | `int` | `5` | Failed sign-ins for one account within the window before it gets 429. |
| `CRYO_AUTH_LOGIN_IP_MAX_FAILURES` | `int` | `20` | Failed sign-ins from one client IP (any account) within the window before it gets 429. Higher than the per-account limit so offices behind one NAT still work. |
| `CRYO_AUTH_LOGIN_WINDOW_SECONDS` | `int` | `900` | Length of the failed sign-in window, and the longest a lockout lasts. |
| `CRYO_API_DOCS_ENABLED` | `bool \| None` | *(unset)* | Serve /docs, /redoc and /openapi.json. Unset means on everywhere except CRYO_ENVIRONMENT=prod, where the schema (every route and model) stays private. |
| `CRYO_METRICS_BEARER_TOKEN` | `str \| None` | *(unset)* | Holds a credential. Set it from a secret store, never from a committed file. When set, the API's root /metrics requires 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' (set bearer_token / credentials in the Prometheus scrape config). Unset keeps it open for in-cluster scrapers; do not route it through a public Ingress. |
| `CRYO_PAGERDUTY_ROUTING_KEY` | `str \| None` | *(unset)* | PagerDuty Events API v2 routing key for high-severity anomalies. |
| `CRYO_WEB_APP_BASE_URL` | `str \| None` | *(unset)* | Base URL of the Cryo web app, used to build deep links in breach alerts. |
| `CRYO_TABLE_ALERT_DISPATCH_INTERVAL_HOURS` | `int` | `1` | Hours between SLA/data-quality breach checks for owned/subscribed tables. |
| `CRYO_TABLE_ALERT_COOLDOWN_HOURS` | `int` | `24` | Minimum hours between repeat breach alerts for the same table. |
| `CRYO_COMMIT_RACE_ALERT_LOOKBACK_HOURS` | `int` | `24` | Window scanned for native compaction runs that lost the optimistic-concurrency commit race (audit detail tagged 'commit_race_lost'); see docs/native-engine-scoping-research.md §3.2. |
| `CRYO_COMMIT_RACE_ALERT_MIN_OCCURRENCES` | `int` | `2` | Number of commit-race losses within the lookback window before a table is flagged as 'compaction losing the commit race'. 1 = alert on the first loss. |
| `CRYO_S3_LOG_INGEST_INTERVAL_HOURS` | `int` | `24` | Hours between S3 request-cost ingestion runs (docs/s3-request-cost-tracking.md §10) -- reads and aggregates every enabled bucket's log objects natively (no Trino/Hive-connector dependency). |
| `CRYO_S3_LOG_INGEST_MAX_OBJECTS_PER_DAY` | `int` | `20000` | Safety cap on how many S3 access-log objects are read per date-partition per ingestion run. A busy bucket can deliver many small per-flush log files; this bounds S3 API call volume per run rather than unbounded object-count growth. Days that hit the cap are logged as a lower-bound (not exact) count, not an error. |
| `CRYO_S3_LOG_INGEST_CONCURRENCY` | `int` | `16` | Max concurrent S3 GetObject calls when reading log objects for a single bucket's ingestion run -- I/O-bound work, so higher than a typical CPU-bound worker pool. |
| `CRYO_LAYOUT_RECOMMENDATION_MAX_TABLES_PER_TICK` | `int` | `20` | Cap on how many tables get a layout-recommendation (re)generated per telemetry tick. generate_layout_recommendation() skips tables refreshed within the last 24h on its own, so this only bounds the cost of the *first* pass over a large backlog -- keeps a single tick from doing thousands of analyses (each with its own bloom-filter/column-stats work) in the same process that already runs the memory-heavy benefit-score updater. Lowered from 200 to 20, 2026-08-14: generate_layout_recommendation() now calls analyze_table_layout(), which -- as of the same date -- self-fetches real per-file column bounds via cryo.optimizer.layout_analyzer.fetch_file_stats (previously a silent no-op, see that function's docstring). Confirmed live: reading one real table's manifests took ~5s; 200 tables/tick at that rate is 15+ minutes of real Iceberg catalog I/O in a single scheduler tick, which this cap now has to actually account for rather than being free. |
| `CRYO_PROPERTY_AUTOPILOT_ENABLED` | `bool` | `false` | Off by default -- opt-in. When true, the scheduler's telemetry tick automatically applies a table's tier1/action=apply property recommendations (metadata-only changes like write.target-file-size-bytes, write.metadata.delete-after-commit.enabled -- never a data rewrite). compute_property_recommendations() and apply_table_properties() were both already fully built and running (the former on a schedule, the latter behind a manual-only API route) but nothing had ever connected them -- confirmed live, 2026-08-10, by grepping the whole codebase for a consumer of the recommendation action field and finding none. See cryo/scanner/property_autopilot.py. |
| `CRYO_PROPERTY_AUTOPILOT_MAX_TABLES_PER_TICK` | `int` | `100` | Cap on how many tables get their safe property recommendations applied per telemetry tick when property_autopilot_enabled is true -- same rationale as layout_recommendation_max_tables_per_tick above: bounds the cost of a single tick rather than trying to sweep the whole fleet in one pass. |
| `CRYO_FAST_PATH_CHECK_ENABLED` | `bool` | `true` | Cheap new-table health sweep on the telemetry tick (RFC Features 2+3). Flags FileDegradationSignal small-file risk and missing write.target-file-size-bytes via compute_property_recommendations; never enqueues optimize. Default on because the work is metadata/stats already in Postgres, not catalog I/O. See cryo/scanner/fast_path_check.py. |
| `CRYO_FAST_PATH_CHECK_MAX_TABLES_PER_TICK` | `int` | `50` | Cap on how many newly discovered tables the fast-path sweep inspects per telemetry tick when fast_path_check_enabled is true. |
| `CRYO_LAYOUT_AUTOPILOT_ENABLED` | `bool` | `false` | Off by default -- opt-in, and a second gate on top of the per-preset opt-in below. When true, the scheduler's telemetry tick automatically approves and executes a table's pending sort/z-order LayoutRecommendation -- but ONLY for tables whose effective preset has params.auto_apply_layout_recommendations = true. Unlike property_autopilot_enabled (tier1, metadata-only, safe fleet-wide by construction), applying a layout recommendation is a real data rewrite (tier2, link_layout) -- see cryo/scanner/property_autopilot.py's tier2 rationale. It stays human-supervised per-table by requiring the preset itself to opt in, not a single global switch, matching the 'test -> adopt & evolve' rollout used for every other autonomy change in this system. See cryo/scheduler/service.py::_run_layout_autopilot. |
| `CRYO_LAYOUT_AUTOPILOT_MAX_TABLES_PER_TICK` | `int` | `20` | Cap on how many tables get their pending layout recommendation auto-executed per telemetry tick when layout_autopilot_enabled is true. Kept far lower than property_autopilot_max_tables_per_tick since each one is a real Spark rewrite job, not a metadata-only property flip. |
| `CRYO_LAYOUT_EFFECTIVENESS_MAX_TABLES_PER_TICK` | `int` | `20` | Cap on how many applied-but-unmeasured LayoutRecommendation rows get a fresh observed_prune_improvement reading per telemetry tick. Always runs (not gated behind an enabled flag like layout_autopilot_enabled) -- unlike actually rewriting a table, measuring an already-applied rewrite's real effect is read-only analysis, no data mutation, safe fleet-wide by construction. See cryo.optimizer.layout_analyzer.measure_layout_recommendation_effectiveness and MIN_HOURS_BEFORE_MEASURING_EFFECTIVENESS for the wait-period rationale. |
| `CRYO_MAX_CONCURRENT_JOBS_PER_METASTORE` | `int` | `150` | Cross-destination cap on RUNNING jobs whose table's source shares the same Hive metastore URI, checked at native-engine admission time. Real incident,  2026-08-12: a Hive metastore OOM'd (heap exhaustion, JvmPauseMonitor and pool-6 threads all throwing OutOfMemoryError) with 322 jobs started in the surrounding 15 minutes and ~70 concurrently failing with literal 'failed to connect to metastore' -- a direct, foreseeable consequence of raising the Governor's per-wave admission throughput (the async fallback-dispatch fix) without checking whether the downstream metastore had headroom for the resulting concurrency. native_datafusion's own slot_cap (e.g. 80) has no relationship to the shared metastore's real connection capacity -- this is a second, independent ceiling, keyed by metastore URI rather than destination since multiple destinations/sources can share one metastore. Deliberately generous (150) rather than tightly tuned -- the goal is a circuit breaker against a repeat of this exact incident, not throughput-optimal metastore sizing, which is the metastore operator's call, not Cryo's. |
| `CRYO_S3_REQUEST_COST_RETENTION_DAYS` | `int` | `35` | Days of S3RequestCostDaily rows kept before the retention job prunes them -- a few days past the 30-day TableCost rollup window. |
| `CRYO_FLEET_ADMISSION_RATE_WINDOW_MINUTES` | `int` | `15` | Rolling window used by fleet_admission_rate_cap -- see that field's docstring for the incident this pair guards against. |
| `CRYO_COST_CEILING_ENABLED` | `bool` | `false` | Enables cryo.reporting.cost_ceiling's real-dollar circuit breaker -- checks the cryo namespace's actual daily spend (used+unused, via Grafana's Athena CUR datasource) and pauses fleet-wide admission (the same MaintenanceControlState global pause an operator's manual pause button writes to) if it exceeds cost_ceiling_daily_usd. Off by default: requires CRYO_GRAFANA_TOKEN to be set (see cryo-secrets) and the scheduler's periodic check to be wired in -- turning this on without that wiring is a silent no-op, not a broken cap, but there's no point defaulting it on before both exist. User-requested, 2026-08-12: a hard $100/day ceiling after real data showed the namespace averaging $210.82/day over the trailing 14 days. |
| `CRYO_COST_CEILING_DAILY_USD` | `float` | `250.0` | Daily used+unused USD ceiling for cost_ceiling_enabled's circuit breaker. Raised 100.0 -> 250.0 2026-09-04: the original $100 (2026-08-12) was calibrated against a namespace that was mostly idle due to since-fixed governor/scheduler bugs -- real spend at healthy throughput (once those fixes shipped and the fleet actually started processing its real backlog) runs ~$150-195/day. $100 left essentially no headroom above normal healthy variance, so trivial day-to-day noise repeatedly tripped a fleet-wide pause. See cost_ceiling_tolerance_pct for the second layer of protection against over-tightening this again. |
| `CRYO_COST_CEILING_TOLERANCE_PCT` | `float` | `0.15` | Fraction above cost_ceiling_daily_usd that's treated as normal variance, not a breach worth halting the fleet for -- e.g. 0.15 means spend up to 15% over the ceiling only logs a warning; only spend beyond that pauses admission. Added 2026-09-04 after a $1.06 overage on a $100 ceiling (1.06% over) triggered a full fleet-wide pause that sat for 4+ hours before a human noticed -- the ceiling had no graduated response, so a rounding-error overage got the identical response as a genuine 5x spend spike. See cryo.reporting.cost_ceiling.enforce_cost_ceiling's own docstring for the full incident. |
| `CRYO_COST_CEILING_CLUSTER_NAME` | `str` | `""` | EKS cluster name as tagged in AWS CUR (resource_tags_aws_eks_cluster_name). Required when cost_ceiling_enabled is true. |
| `CRYO_COST_CEILING_NAMESPACE` | `str` | `cryo` | Kubernetes namespace to check against cost_ceiling_daily_usd. |
| `CRYO_COST_CEILING_CHECK_INTERVAL_MINUTES` | `int` | `30` | How often the scheduler re-checks real spend. CUR data lags 24-48h, so checking much more often than this doesn't reveal new information -- this mainly controls how quickly a pause gets lifted once yesterday's lagged data catches up to show spend back under the ceiling. |
| `CRYO_GRAFANA_ATHENA_DATASOURCE_UID` | `str` | `""` | Grafana datasource uid for the Athena CUR connection used by the cost ceiling. Required when cost_ceiling_enabled or Trino scan-cost pricing is on. |
| `CRYO_GRAFANA_BASE_URL` | `str` | `""` | Base URL for cost_ceiling's Grafana API calls, no trailing slash. Required when cost_ceiling_enabled is true. |
| `CRYO_TRINO_COST_PRICING_ENABLED` | `bool` | `false` | Enables deriving a real $/GiB Trino compute price from the trino-db namespace's actual Grafana Athena CUR cost (cryo.reporting.cost_ceiling.fetch_namespace_cost_range) divided by real bytes scanned that day (QueryCostAttributionDaily's rollup), and writing it onto QueryCostAttributionDaily.estimated_scan_cost_usd -- previously left NULL everywhere, since Trino-on-EKS has no published per-byte price the way S3 does. Off by default: same CRYO_GRAFANA_TOKEN dependency as cost_ceiling_enabled, and turning this on without that secret set is a silent no-op, not a broken feature. |
| `CRYO_TRINO_COST_PRICING_NAMESPACE` | `str` | `trino-db` | Kubernetes namespace to price against (see trino_cost_pricing_enabled). |
| `CRYO_TRINO_COST_PRICING_LOOKBACK_DAYS` | `int` | `10` | How many trailing days to (re-)price on each tick. Wider than CUR's 24-48h lag on purpose, so a day whose cost data was still incomplete on a prior tick gets priced once it catches up, not stuck NULL forever. |
| `CRYO_FLEET_ADMISSION_RATE_CAP` | `int` | `500` | Blunt, mechanism-agnostic ceiling on total jobs (any status, any destination, fleet-wide) admitted within fleet_admission_rate_window_minutes. Real incident, 2026-08-11 evening: 11,824 native jobs ran in one day, with 100+ admitted in single-minute windows and 31% of the day's jobs failing -- the metastore-concurrency cap (max_concurrent_jobs_per_metastore) and the concurrent-write-race fix (native_admit.py's snapshot-mutation defer) both close specific mechanisms that burst caused, but neither bounds the burst itself -- a different downstream bottleneck could still choke on the same admission volume. This is the backstop: if the fleet is admitting jobs this fast, something is already wrong (a retry storm, a misconfigured preset re-firing, an operator's bulk trigger) and it's worth pausing new admissions rather than richocheting straight through cluster capacity into whatever breaks next. Deliberately generous (500 per 15min = ~33/min average, well above the ~44/min peak throughput the async fallback-dispatch fix was built to reach) -- this is a circuit breaker against a repeat of the exact 2026-08-11 burst shape, not a throughput limiter for normal operation. |
| `CRYO_ANOMALY_DETECTION_BATCH_SIZE` | `int` | `100` | Tables processed per batch in fleet-wide anomaly detection. |
| `CRYO_ANOMALY_HISTORY_ROWS_PER_TABLE` | `int` | `60` | Max history rows loaded per table during anomaly detection. |
| `CRYO_ANOMALY_MAX_RESULTS` | `int` | `500` | Maximum anomaly alerts retained from a fleet-wide scan. |
| `CRYO_PUFFIN_LOCAL_DIR` | `str` | `.local/puffin` | On-disk directory for Puffin blobs in local dev (CRYO_PUFFIN_LOCAL_DIR). |
| `CRYO_SILENT_LOSS_CHECK_INTERVAL_MIN` | `int` | `5` | Minutes between silent-data-loss scans per table (CRYO_SILENT_LOSS_CHECK_INTERVAL_MIN). |
| `CRYO_SILENT_LOSS_LOCAL_ROOT` | `str` | `.local/tables` | Local filesystem root for table data in dev (CRYO_SILENT_LOSS_LOCAL_ROOT). |
| `CRYO_SILENT_LOSS_BATCH_SIZE` | `int` | `500` | Tables swept per scheduler tick by the silent-data-loss sweep, not the whole fleet at once -- sweeping ~13k tables unbounded in one session accumulated every Table/TableStats ORM object simultaneously and OOMKilled cryo-scheduler every ~5min in production. The sweep rotates through the fleet across ticks instead (CRYO_SILENT_LOSS_BATCH_SIZE). |

| `CRYO_QPP_FAIL_OPEN` | `bool` | `false` | When true, a QPP prediction error admits the job (advisory-only deployments). By default an error defers the job with reason qpp_gate_check_failed, the same fail-closed behaviour as the PII gate. |
| `CRYO_QPP_TARGET_P95_MS` | `int` | `600000` | Default per-destination QPP p95 target in milliseconds. |
| `CRYO_QPP_MIN_OBSERVATIONS` | `int` | `20` | Minimum observations before QPPModel trusts the learned regression. |
| `CRYO_OBSERVATION_LAKEHOUSE_PATH` | `str` | `.local/observations` | On-disk path where the observation lakehouse stores long-term actuations. |
| `CRYO_LLM_DEFAULT_MODEL_ANTHROPIC` | `str` | `claude-sonnet-4-20250514` | Default Anthropic model when provider row omits model. |
| `CRYO_LLM_DEFAULT_MODEL_OPENAI` | `str` | `gpt-4o` | Default OpenAI model when provider row omits model. |

| `CRYO_LLM_OPENAI_BASE_URL` | `str \| None` | *(unset)* | Optional OpenAI-compatible API base override (vLLM/Ollama/local gateways). When set, OpenAI provider calls are routed through this endpoint. A non-OpenAI/Azure origin is used only if it is listed in CRYO_LLM_ALLOWED_ORIGINS. |

| `CRYO_LLM_DAILY_TOKEN_CAP_DEFAULT` | `int` | `300000` | Holds a credential. Set it from a secret store, never from a committed file. Default per-provider daily token cap when provider budget omits it. |
| `CRYO_LLM_DAILY_COST_CAP_USD_DEFAULT` | `float` | `15.0` | Default per-provider daily spend cap in USD (best-effort; derived from provider config pricing). |
| `CRYO_LLM_OVER_BUDGET_MODE` | `Literal` | `abstain` | Behavior when an LLM provider exceeds budget: hard reject or abstain-with-fallback. |
| `CRYO_AI_FEATURE_DIAGNOSIS_ENABLED` | `bool` | `true` | Enable run-failure diagnosis API/UI surfaces. |
| `CRYO_AI_FEATURE_FILTER_TRANSLATION_ENABLED` | `bool` | `true` | Enable natural-language table-filter translation. |
| `CRYO_AI_FEATURE_PLAN_NARRATION_ENABLED` | `bool` | `true` | Enable optional plan narration for SQL intent in PlanPreview. |
| `CRYO_AI_FEATURE_ANOMALY_BRIEF_ENABLED` | `bool` | `true` | Enable anomaly root-cause brief surfaces. |
| `CRYO_MCP_RUN_PRESET_ENABLED` | `bool` | `false` | Allow write-capable MCP run_preset tool. Disabled by default for safety. |
| `CRYO_ASSISTANT_ENABLED` | `bool` | `false` | Master switch for Ask Cryo. Stays off until an operator enables it. |
| `CRYO_ASSISTANT_WRITES_ENABLED` | `bool` | `false` | Assistant-only kill switch, separate from maintenance_writes_enabled. |
| `CRYO_ASSISTANT_MAX_TOOL_CALLS` | `int` | `8` | - |
| `CRYO_ASSISTANT_MAX_PARALLEL_READS` | `int` | `4` | - |
| `CRYO_ASSISTANT_TURN_TIMEOUT_S` | `int` | `45` | - |
| `CRYO_ASSISTANT_PROPOSAL_TTL_S` | `int` | `600` | - |
| `CRYO_ASSISTANT_MAX_ACTIVE_TURNS_PER_USER` | `int` | `2` | - |
| `CRYO_ASSISTANT_RETENTION_DAYS` | `int` | `90` | - |
| `CRYO_ASSISTANT_MCP_ENABLED` | `bool` | `false` | Expose the streamable HTTP MCP adapter. Off until BOT-09 is qualified. |
| `CRYO_PLAN_VERIFIER_ENABLED` | `bool` | `true` | When false, /plans/verify and the enqueue-time verifier pass-through return 503. Lets ops kill the feature without redeploying. |
| `CRYO_DURABLE_INTENTS_ENABLED` | `bool` | `false` | Bind new maintenance jobs to immutable plans, monotonic table fences, attempts, and effect receipts. Safety-alpha migration flag; legacy jobs remain executable. |
| `CRYO_DURABLE_INTENT_TTL_HOURS` | `int` | `24` | Maximum time a bound maintenance intent remains executable. Scheduled intents start their TTL at scheduled dispatch time and are also capped by the run deadline. |
| `CRYO_ROI_GATE_ENABLED` | `bool` | `false` | Enable ROI-based governor gate for maintenance admission decisions. |
| `CRYO_ROI_GATE_SHADOW_MODE` | `bool` | `true` | Log ROI decisions without enforcing skip/defer while tuning thresholds. |
| `CRYO_ROI_MIN_BCR` | `float` | `1.0` | Minimum benefit-cost ratio required for non-streaming tables. |
| `CRYO_ROI_MIN_BCR_STREAMING` | `float` | `0.5` | Minimum benefit-cost ratio required for streaming/hot tables. |
| `CRYO_ROI_SHADOW_MIN_SAMPLES` | `int` | `200` | Minimum shadow decisions before suggesting ROI enforcement. |
| `CRYO_GOVERNOR_BANDIT_TUNING_ENABLED` | `bool` | `false` | When true, a Thompson-sampling bandit may override the admission config an operator set on a destination (per_replica_cap, high_load_ratio/fraction, default_cooldown_hours, min_benefit_score) and learning signals are recorded on every admission and deferral. Off by default because both halves were costly: admission became non-deterministic -- the concurrency cap was resampled every wave, so the same fleet state could admit a different amount each time, which makes the governor's behaviour unreproducible exactly when it is being debugged -- and recording did a load-modify-save of one Postgres row per job, so a wave deferring 800 jobs meant ~1,600 round trips and 800 commits contending on that single row, plus a read-modify-write of a node-local JSON file per admission that multiple governor replicas cannot keep consistent. The knobs it tunes are ones the operator already sets explicitly per destination. |
| `CRYO_GOVERNOR_SHADOW_SAMPLE_RATE` | `int` | `20` | Evaluate the ROI-gate and resource-predictor shadow paths for 1 in N candidates per wave, not every one. Live-verified 2026-09-02: both paths do 2-3 real DB queries per candidate purely to log a shadow recommendation neither currently enforces (roi_gate_shadow_mode's own log-then-fall-through branch, and the resource predictor has no enforcement path at all yet) -- at ~800 candidates in a large wave that's 3000+ synchronous round-trips per wave for data nobody acts on, found to be the dominant remaining cost after the two unbounded-reconcile-scan bugs fixed the same day were resolved. Sampling keeps shadow-mode data collection alive (roi_shadow_min_samples's 200-sample target is still reached well within a single large wave at this rate) without paying the full per-candidate cost on every wave. 1 disables sampling (evaluates every candidate, the pre-fix behavior). |
| `CRYO_FORECAST_WINDOW_DAYS` | `int` | `14` | Historical window used by EWMA workload forecaster. |
| `CRYO_FORECAST_DEFAULT_HORIZON_HOURS` | `int` | `24` | Default workload forecast horizon for smart-maintenance API endpoints. |
